To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrolases found in pulmonary lavage effluants are not derived from cell leakage but rather from lamellar bodies of type 2 cells.
the hydrolases obtained in lavage effluent are of a selected variety and are probably derived from lamellar bodies.
the extracellular enzymes in pulmonary lavage effluants are derived from lamellar bodies of type 2 alveolar cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, isolation and characterization of the enzymes associated with the lamellar bodies of the type 2 alveolar cells.
the identification, quantitation and localization of the hydrolases found within the acellular lung lining fluid.
the identification, isolation, and characterization of the enzymes of the lung, with special reference to the hydrolases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
extracellular hydroses in the lung originate from the type 2 cell.
the extracellular acid hydrolase pool of the lung is derived from the lamellar bodies of type 2 cells and is not due to leakage of serum or cell damage.
the extracellular acid hydrolase pool in the lung is derived from lamellar bodies and that the type 2 cell is the major contributor of these enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrolase content of the lamellar body is determined by the type 1 cell and is then selected by the type II cell for secretion.
the hydrolases present in the alveolar lining material of the lung are not of serum or cell origin but are derived from lamellar bodies of the pulmonary type 2 cell.
extracellular hydralases of the lung are of lysosomal origin, are selected from lysosome-free lamellae and are not derived by leakage from damaged cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hydrolases from the lysosomal system are secreted into the extracellular space in the lung.
the extracellular acid hydrolase pool in the lung may be derived directly from lamellar bodies.

the extracellular enzymes of the lung are not simply a reflection of the enzymes found in serum, but rather are a selected group of hydrolases that are derived from the lamellar bodies of type 2 cells.
